SANKHYA v1.0.0, the LP / MILP / convex QP solver written from scratch for Smart India Hackathon 2026, problem statement SIH26119 (Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd). 197 commits on `main` since v1.0.0-rc5, these notes included.

## Download

| asset | for |
|---|---|
| `sankhya-1.0.0-linux-x86_64-cpu.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64, glibc 2.35 or later |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-linux-x86_64-cuda.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64 with an NVIDIA driver; the CUDA runtime is linked in |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-windows-x64-cpu.zip` | Windows 10 / 11 x64 |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-windows-x64-cuda.zip` | Windows 10 / 11 x64 with an NVIDIA driver; the CUDA runtime and cuSPARSE DLLs are beside the binary |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl` | `pip install` on Linux x86-64, CPython 3.9 to 3.13 |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-win_amd64.whl` | `pip install` on Windows x64, CPython 3.9 to 3.13 |
| `sankhya-image.tar.gz` | the container image, for `docker load` offline |
| `SHA256SUMS` | over every archive and wheel |

No compiler is needed. Unpack an archive, then from the unpacked directory:

    build/sankhya version
    build/sankhya solve demo/crude_blend.mps --write-sol blend.sol
    python3 tools/verify_solution.py demo/crude_blend.mps blend.sol
    demo/finale.sh                     # Windows: demo\finale.cmd

Python, straight from this release (nothing is on PyPI):

    pip install https://github.com/thegoodengineers/SANKHYA/releases/download/v1.0.0/sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl
    # Windows: .../v1.0.0/sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-win_amd64.whl
    python -c "import sankhya; print(sankhya.Model.read('demo/crude_blend.mps').solve().objective)"

Container (CUDA build, the verifier and the demo models):

    docker pull ghcr.io/thegoodengineers/sankhya:v1.0.0
    docker run --rm --gpus all ghcr.io/thegoodengineers/sankhya:v1.0.0 sankhya solve demo/crude_blend.mps --gpu

Check a download against `SHA256SUMS`. Each archive's `MANIFEST.txt` records the commit, compiler and CUDA toolkit it was built with and the libraries it links; CI fails the packaging if any of them is an optimization solver.

## Wrong answers found and fixed since rc5

The most important change in this release. A general-form fuzz against an exact rational oracle (#1334, now on every pull request) and a line-by-line audit of the code found the defects below. Each fix landed with a test that failed on `main` in CI before it and passes after it.

- **Wrong optimum, default path:**
  - presolve snapped an integer column's implied bound in the wrong units (#1319);
  - a node was closed on an integral point the incumbent test had refused (#1312);
  - integral-row rounding treated coefficients within 1e-6 of an integer as integers (#1341);
  - node propagation rounded an implied bound past its rounding error, and summed a bound of 1e20 or 1e30 as a number (#1359, #1360);
  - presolve fixed a column whose box was under 1e-7 wide, and substituted a two-entry ranged row under 1e-7 wide as an equation (#1362, #1363);
  - a non-convex QP whose large diagonal hid negative curvature was solved as convex, and a saddle point was returned (#1369).
- **Wrong status:**
  - an unbounded LP was reported feasible after presolve fixed a column off an empty dual box (#1337);
  - an infeasible MILP whose relaxation is unbounded was reported unbounded (#1343);
  - an infeasible MILP was reported as a model error (#1335);
  - a feasible MILP ended in a numerical error when its node point was feasible only in scaled units (#1348);
  - the Farkas and ray checkers accepted false proofs of infeasibility and unboundedness (#1371, #1370).
- **Misread models:**
  - `0x1` in an LP file was read as the hexadecimal number 1 (#1366);
  - the LP format's Binary section unfixed a binary its Bounds section had fixed (#1367);
  - MPS `QSECTION` went to the objective whatever row it named, and a quadratic record's second entry was dropped (#1368).
- **Opt-in paths:**
  - parallel rows (`presolve_parallel_rows`) and implied-free substitution (`presolve_implied_free`), under the engine race or not (#1339, #1350, #1354, #1364).
- **A regression the fixes exposed, fixed before this release:**
  - with narrow boxes kept, postsolve could report a basis status 4e-5 off its bound, and a phase-2 cycle could run to the time limit (#1389).

## Other changes since rc5

- **QP:**
  - A Ruiz-equilibration retry when the interior point stalls (#1381), on by default: qpilotno and stadat1 now solve.
  - Dense nodes are ordered last in the QP interior point's factorization (#1357), on by default: boyd1 from 31.7 s to 3.4 s.
  - The dual regularization drops to its floor where every row has a slack (#1284): liswet8, 9 and 12 reach optimal; liswet8 is still not counted as passed, because its published value is a recorded erratum (#1180).
- **Global (non-convex bilinear):**
  - Reformulation-linearization rows on by default (#1283, #1291) and root bound tightening behind `global_obbt` (#1290).
  - The lift of a P-formulated pool to the Q-formulation, behind `global_pool_lift` (#1388).
  - A refinery gasoline pooling case study solved globally and checked by two independent tools.
- **MILP:**
  - The root cut loop gated on flow covers, with the cut pool and lifted aggregated flow covers, on by default (#1158).
  - Probing in rounds, and its integer bounds kept where it fixes a fifth of the integer columns.
  - Probing keeps row activities, so a probe passes over rows that cannot imply anything (#1347).
  - `mip_threads` is one tree worker per core, up to 4.
  - The node factor cache, and the LU workspace kept between probes.
  - A time budget per dive, and the parity heuristic gated on how much it fixes.
  - `mip_heuristics=auto`: the optional heuristics run until the first incumbent.
- **LP:**
  - The textbook dual ratio test takes no backward step (#1325), and refuted primal optimality claims end on fresh factors (#1327).
  - Each work vector keeps its support, so no dual step costs O(m).
  - Network-shaped LPs stay on the dual simplex.
  - The crossover from an optimal interior point gets half the time left.
  - PDHG runs on to the project's standard by default.
- **Scenarios:** one model under many cost and right-hand-side sets, warm-started, through the C API and Python, every answer verified independently (#752).
- **Tooling:**
  - `bench.yml` A/Bs run both arms on one binary in one job, and the stress, infeasible and QPLIB suites run in CI.
  - The PuLP and Pyomo adapters report LP duals.

| Maros-Meszaros, 138 convex QPs, 60 s | 131 passed (matched within 1e-6 and verified), 137 verified | 45913772693, #1381's head |

The CSVs are in each run's artifact. The release commit's own full re-run is committed to `bench/results/` after the tag, and `README.md` and `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` are regenerated from it.

## Limits, stated

- **MIPLIB 2017 is the gap.** On the whole 240-model benchmark set at 60 s SANKHYA proves 7, HiGHS 52 (`miplib2017-bench-60s-3dba456.csv`). On MIPLIB 3 SANKHYA is fourth of the five named solvers (HiGHS 50, CBC 48, SCIP 46, SANKHYA 44, GLPK 32; `head-to-head-miplib3-60s-5ce0630.csv`).
- **Large LPs:** 8 of 16 on Mittelmann's LP set at 600 s, and the Kennington shifted geometric mean time is behind HiGHS's.
- **The fixes cost some MILP proofs:** on MIPLIB 3 the rounding margin that stops the #1360 wrong answers costs gesa2_o two proofs and 10teams one (seeds 1 and 2); best of three is unchanged at 46.
- **QP:** of the 7 Maros-Meszaros QPs not passed, values is not convex (correctly refused), and hues-mod, huestis and liswet8 differ from published values that are recorded errata (#1078, #1180). qforplan, qgfrdxpn and qshell end `feasible`: the verifier refuses their reduced costs at the rounding of their terms.
- **GPU:** the CUDA archives and the GPU engines are not re-measured for this release. The Windows CUDA kernels have not run on a Windows machine with a card.
- **Platforms:** one wheel per platform, Linux x86-64 and Windows x64 only; no macOS, no aarch64, nothing on PyPI.

The full evidence, including what does not work, is in `README.md`, `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` and `docs/NEGATIVE-RESULTS.md` at the tagged commit.
